channel.title: Orion Duarte: All the Latest Rock and Metal News on Loud Legends
channel.description: Recent content in Orion Duarte: All the Latest Rock and Metal News on Loud Legends

item.title: Jack White of The White Stripes Slams Trump Over Redskins Name Flip-Flop
item.description: Jack White, known for his work with The White Stripes and a long solo career, is calling out former President Donald Trump over two contradictory posts about the Washington NFL team’s name.

item.title: The Guitarist ANGUS YOUNG Once Blamed For Setting ROCK MUSIC Back Two Decades: 'Jeez, It Sounds So Dated'
item.description: Angus Young , the longtime AC/DC guitarist, is known for his stripped-down style, blistering riffs, and no-nonsense views on what makes a good guitar player. Over the years, he’s made his opinion clear about effects pedals, tremolo bars, and overly polished guitar work.

item.title: JANE’S ADDICTION Bandmates Sue PERRY FARRELL for 10 Million Over Onstage Fight; FARRELL Responds With Countersuit Alleging Years of Bullying and Harassment
item.description: Members of the rock band Jane’s Addiction have filed a $10 million lawsuit against frontman Perry Farrell, following a public onstage fight in Boston that ended their 2024 reunion tour (via Rolling Stone).

item.title: Brent Smith Says ‘The Audience Is the Boss’ as Shinedown Releases New Single ‘Killing Fields’; Watch
item.description: Shinedown has released a new single called Killing Fields (listen below). The track is now available on all major streaming platforms. It was released through Atlantic Records.

item.title: CRYPTA’s Luana Dametto to Play Drums at VIMIC’s October 3 Tribute to Joey Jordison
item.description: VIMIC, the metal band formed by the late Joey Jordison after his departure from Slipknot, will reunite for a special tribute concert in Los Angeles. The show is set for October 3 at the Teragram Ballroom and will feature Luana Dametto, drummer of Brazilian death metal band Crypta, filling in on drums.

item.title: KELLY OSBOURNE Doesn’t Hold Back After Bizarre VIRAL AI Video Claims OZZY and SHARON Made a Private End-of-Life Decision
item.description: Kelly Osbourne is setting the record straight about her parents, Ozzy and Sharon Osbourne. The TV personality and daughter of the legendary rocker addressed growing rumors on social media suggesting that her parents had entered a so-called “suicide pact” to end their lives together if their health deteriorated.

item.title: NIKKI SIXX Reveals Why MÖTLEY CRÜE Were Missing From OZZY OSBOURNE’s Farewell Show
item.description: Fans of Mötley Crüe noticed something missing during Ozzy Osbourne’s massive Back to the Beginning farewell concert in Birmingham: the Crüe themselves. The event, held on July 5, was billed as a once-in-a-lifetime celebration.

item.title: Is This How It Ends? AARON STAINTHORPE Unsure If He’s Still the Vocalist of MY DYING BRIDE
item.description: Aaron Stainthorpe isn’t entirely sure whether he’s still the lead singer of My Dying Bride. The British doom metal band recently returned to the stage with Mikko Kotamäki, from Swallow the Sun, handling vocals.

item.title: Deftones Announce 2026 European and UK Tour With Denzel Curry and Drug Church
item.description: Deftones are heading back to Europe in 2026. The Sacramento-based alternative metal band has confirmed a 15-date arena tour across Europe and the United Kingdom in support of their upcoming album Private Music.

item.title: JOHN BUSH Explains Why He Rejected METALLICA: 'They Were Nobodies Back Then'
item.description: John Bush, best known for fronting Armored Saint and later Anthrax, recently spoke in depth about the time he was offered a spot as Metallica’s lead singer.

item.title: SHARON OSBOURNE Teased A Post-Show Reveal About The Band She Banned From OZZY's Farewell, But We Might Already Know Who It Is
item.description: For a concert billed as Back to the Beginning, meant to close the book on the legacy of Black Sabbath and mark Ozzy Osbourne’s final bow, one detail stood out more for what was missing than what was onstage.

item.title: KELLY OSBOURNE and SID WILSON Get Engaged at OZZY OSBOURNE’s Final BLACK SABBATH Concert; VIDEO
item.description: Kelly Osbourne and Sid Wilson are officially engaged. The couple marked the occasion in a memorable way, with the proposal happening backstage at none other than Ozzy Osbourne’s final concert with Black Sabbath.

item.title: FOO FIGHTERS Release 'TODAY’S SONG' Ahead of Album’s 30th Anniversary; VIDEO
item.description: Foo Fighters have released a new track titled “Today’s Song” (watch below) to celebrate the upcoming 30th anniversary of their self-titled debut album. The single is available now on major streaming platforms.

item.title: OZZY OSBOURNE Confirms Live Retirement: 'It’s A Goodbye As Far As My Live Performances Go'
item.description: In a new interview promoting this weekend’s Back to the Beginning event, the legendary Black Sabbath frontman confirmed that his upcoming concert at Villa Park in Birmingham, England, will be his final time performing live.

item.title: OZZY OSBOURNE Launches Limited Makeup Line With Jolie Beauty
item.description: The rock legend has partnered with Jolie Beauty, an independent makeup brand based in Birmingham, U.K., to create a limited-edition collection of cosmetics. The collection will go on sale starting July 9 through the Jolie Beauty website.

item.title: FAITH NO MORE’s Mike Bordin Says OZZY OSBOURNE Saved His Life: 'You’re the reason I’m here'
item.description: When Faith No More released The Real Thing in June 1989, it marked more than just their third studio album. It was the first with vocalist Mike Patton and quickly became a defining moment for the band.

item.title: What ANGUS YOUNG Thinks About Fans Who Rejected AXL ROSE As AC/DC’s Singer
item.description: In an interview with Rolling Stone in 2021, guitarist Angus Young opened up about a moment that split fans of AC/DC, when Axl Rose stepped in as lead singer during their 2016 tour.

item.title: KIRK HAMMETT Opens Up About Comparing Himself To New Guitarists: 'Where Did I Go Wrong? I Should Be Much Better'
item.description: Kirk Hammett might have four decades with Metallica under his belt, but if you ask him, he’s not exactly resting on his reputation. In a recent interview with Metal Hammer, the longtime guitarist was asked to reflect on how he sees himself as a player.

item.title: HOLLYWOOD UNDEAD Releases Emotional New Single 'SAVIOR': 'We Can’t Wait For You To Hear It'
item.description: Rock group Hollywood Undead has dropped a new single titled “Savior” (watch it below), offering fans a more personal and emotional look at the band’s sound. The track is out now through Sumerian Records.

item.title: Dream Theater's MIKE PORTNOY Defends LARS ULRICH: 'He Takes a Beating, But He's Invaluable'
item.description: Mike Portnoy, drummer for Dream Theater, says Lars Ulrich deserves more credit. In a recent chat with El Estepario Siberiano (transcribed by LOUDLEGENDS.COM), Portnoy explained why he thinks the Metallica co-founder is often misunderstood.

item.title: The One Drummer PHIL COLLINS Admired But Called Out For Having A Massive Ego: 'The Size of a Hotel'
item.description: Phil Collins wasn’t just the voice that brought pop stardom to Genesis. He also helped redefine how drums were recorded in the 1980s, built a massive solo career, and even teamed up with unexpected names, like when he played with Led Zeppelin.

item.title: Mick Ralphs, Co-Founder of Bad Company and Mott the Hoople, Dies at 81
item.description: Mick Ralphs, the guitarist and songwriter who helped shape the sound of classic rock with Bad Company and Mott the Hoople, has died at age 81. He is survived by his partner, Susie Chavasse, his two sons, three stepchildren, and his longtime bandmates Paul Rodgers and Simon Kirke.

item.title: The BLACK SABBATH Song That Blew Led Zeppelin's JOHN BONHAM’s Mind
item.description: Before joining Led Zeppelin and becoming a rock legend, John Bonham was already turning heads in the music scene of England’s Black Country. As a teenager, just 16 years old, he crossed paths with a fellow drummer: Bill Ward, who would later power Black Sabbath’s thunderous rhythm section.

item.title: The RUSH Album That Led to Fan Backlash, Internal Tension, and a Moment of Regret: 'It Wasn’t the Smartest Move'
item.description: Most bands with long careers eventually take a creative detour. Whether to keep things fresh or avoid burnout, they try something new. Sometimes it works. Sometimes it doesn’t.

item.title: AARON STAINTHORPE Talks Leaving MY DYING BRIDE: 'I Feel 10 Years Younger'
item.description: Aaron Stainthorpe, known for fronting British metal band My Dying Bride for over three decades, says his new project has given him a fresh perspective, and a second wind.

item.title: The AC/DC album that FLOPPED HARDER Than Expected And Nearly Turned Into A FULL-BLOWN CRISIS
item.description: Back in Black is the album everyone knows. It’s the one that sold like crazy and turned AC/DC into a global powerhouse. But not every album had the same luck.

item.title: SCOTT STAPP Says CREED Is Rebuilding: 'We're Talking About New Music'
item.description: CREED frontman Scott Stapp says the band is easing back into things after more than a decade apart. In a recent interview, he shared that the group has been spending time together, reflecting on the past, and having early conversations about making new music (via Meltdown) (transcribed by BLABBERMOUTH.

item.title: THE BAND That Toured With Guns N’ Roses and Wished They Hadn’t: 'I Don’t Want To Be Around Them'
item.description: In the early ’90s, opening for Guns N’ Roses was considered a golden ticket, massive crowds, media buzz, and a shot at mainstream fame. For Soundgarden, a loud and rising band from Seattle, the offer felt like a fast pass out of the grunge underground.

item.title: The Unusual Way AC/DC's ANGUS YOUNG Came Up With the Chorus of 'HIGHWAY TO HELL'
item.description: Angus Young, lead guitarist and founding member of AC/DC, shared a rather unexpected story about how he wrote one of rock’s most iconic choruses. Speaking in a 2021 interview with Essentials Radio on Apple Music (via Kerrang), Young explained how the chorus of “Highway to Hell” came to him, not in a studio or during rehearsal, but while he was on a bathroom break.

item.title: The One Thing That Could End MEGADETH, According to DAVE MUSTAINE
item.description: Megadeth has been going strong for four decades, led from day one by guitarist, vocalist, and founding member Dave Mustaine. He’s the only constant in the thrash metal band’s long history and the driving force behind many of its best-known songs, including “Peace Sells,” “In My Darkest Hour,” “Holy Wars… The Punishment Due,” “Symphony of Destruction,” “A Tout Le Monde,” and “Trust.

item.title: The 'COMMERCIAL' Song AC/DC Didn’t Want To Record, And It Ended Up On The Charts
item.description: In June 1978, AC/DC got their first taste of chart action in the UK with “Rock ’n’ Roll Damnation”, which reached number 24. Nothing to throw a parade over, but for a band that had never cracked the charts there before, it was a decent showing.

item.title: THREE DAYS GRACE Releases New Single 'DOMINATE' Ahead Of Upcoming Album
item.description: Three Days Grace has released a new single titled “Dominate” (watch the video at the end of the article), available today on all major streaming platforms. The track is part of the band’s upcoming eighth studio album, Alienation, scheduled for release on August 22, 2025, via RCA Records.

item.title: JAMES HETFIELD On the 'Weak' METALLICA Member: 'Not Amazing'
item.description: James Hetfield has always been particular when it comes to Metallica’s music. Known for his precision as a rhythm guitarist, he’s often regarded as the most technically sharp member of the band, along with current bassist Robert Trujillo.

item.title: PAUL STANLEY On KISS Reunion Regrets: 'Some Nights Were Awful'
item.description: Turns out the face paint couldn’t cover everything. Back in 2000, KISS slapped the word farewell on a tour, grabbed the original lineup, and hit the road like it was 1977 all over again.

item.title: KORN Praises SLEEP TOKEN's Download Festival Show: 'They Outdid a SLIPKNOT Stage'
item.description: The members of Korn had high praise for Sleep Token following their performance at the Download Festival on Saturday, June 14. According to the band, the masked group managed to silence skeptics with a massive stage setup and commanding live presence.

item.title: IHSAHN Explains Why GHOST, SLEEP TOKEN And SLIPKNOT Attract Crowds: 'It's The Masks, The Visuals, The Mystery'
item.description: Ihsahn has no interest in blurring the lines between personal life and stage persona. In his opinion, keeping those worlds apart explains why bands like Ghost, Sleep Token, and Slipknot generate such obsessive fascination.

item.title: Michael Wilton Talks New Queensrÿche Album and 2025 Goals
item.description: Queensrÿche guitarist Michael Wilton spoke with Robert Cavuoto (for MyGlobalMind). Touched on new record plans? Absolutely. Also reflected on the many twists and turns the band has faced over the decades (and there have been plenty).

item.title: Necrobutcher on Mayhem's Four Decades of Survival
item.description: When the bassist of your band murders the guitarist, you’d think the group might call it quits. Most bands implode over petty squabbles about songwriting credits or tour schedules—not criminal trials.

item.title: Watch: RAMMSTEIN Shares Exclusive Tour Documentary; VIDEO
item.description: RAMMSTEIN’s World Stadium Tour 2019–2024 documentary is here, clocking in at just under an hour. For a band that’s made an entire career out of fire, leather, and eyebrow-scorching theatrics, they’ve now decided to show us the real magic—spoiler alert: it’s the crew hauling stage pieces like they’re building the pyramids.

item.title: Tim Lambesis Faces Solo Challenge as As I Lay Dying Joins Rockville 2025
item.description: The lineup for Welcome to Rockville 2025 has been rolling out steadily, but one name caught more than a few raised eyebrows this weekend—As I Lay Dying. For those not keeping score, the band is now essentially just Tim Lambesis.

item.title: Welcome to Rockville 2025 Books As I Lay Dying Despite Chaos
item.description: The wreckage that is 2024 As I Lay Dying looks more like a construction zone than a band these days, but apparently, that’s not stopping Tim Lambesis from slapping the name on a festival poster.

item.title: Linkin Park Announces From Zero Listening Events Across U.S.
item.description: Linkin Park is at it again, boys and girls—this time with listening events scattered across over 100 U.S. record stores for their new album, From Zero. Scheduled for Saturday, November 9, these events give fans a sneak peek at the record before it officially hits shelves on Friday, November 15.

item.title: Band Exodus: As I Lay Dying Loses Three Members in One Week
item.description: The slow-motion collapse of what’s left of As I Lay Dying keeps unraveling. It began with bassist and clean vocalist Ryan Neff deciding to call it quits earlier this week.

item.title: KEN SUSI Walks Away from AS I LAY DYING: "My Morals Hit Their Limit"
item.description: The As I Lay Dying ship seems to be taking on water—fast. First, bassist Ryan Neff jumped overboard, offering little more than a vague farewell. Then whispers started about their European tour vanishing into thin air, allegedly after their tour manager quit.

item.title: Ryan Neff Exits As I Lay Dying: Another Chapter in the Band’s Soap Opera
item.description: Bassist and vocalist Ryan Neff decided his time with As I Lay Dying was short-lived, officially announcing his departure on October 18. The timing? Right before the band gears up for a sprawling European tour.

item.title: Ice Nine Kills Drummer Patrick Galante Steps Down
item.description: Ice Nine Kills just lost a piece of their rhythm section, and no, it’s not some dramatic ‘spooky’ horror movie twist. Patrick Galante, who’s been holding down the drum kit since 2018, has decided to hang up his sticks—at least with INK.

item.title: Shavo Odadjian’s Seven Hours After Violet Drops New Single "Cry"; VIDEO
item.description: Shavo Odadjian is back with his new project—SEVEN HOURS AFTER VIOLET—and they’ve just dropped the music video for their latest single, “Cry.” Far from being a System of a Down copycat, this track goes straight into anguish, longing, and all the good ol’ despair you’d expect from a song called “Cry.

item.title: Mick Thomson on Slipknot’s First Album: “My Solos Were Cut”
item.description: Slipknot’s first album is a maelstrom of riffs, rage, and pure chaos, but here’s a tidbit you might’ve missed: not a single guitar solo survived the final cut.

item.title: Cliff Burton's Spirit Lives On in Metallica's Music, Says James Hetfield
item.description: James Hetfield still hears Cliff Burton’s voice. Not literally, but in his head when he’s writing music. During a recent episode of “The Metallica Report”, the frontman was asked if Cliff still influences his work.

item.title: Evanescence to Begin Recording New Album in November
item.description: Evanescence—masters of gothic drama and mid-2000s radio dominance—is gearing up to record their next album. When? November. (Mark your calendars, or don’t. Your call.) The news dropped during an interview with 89 A Rádio Rock at Rock In Rio, where the band is currently melting faces.

item.title: Metallica Confirms 2025 Headline Tour with Iconic Support Acts
item.description: Metallica is rolling out a 2025 North American tour, bringing their mix of old-school riffs and new album jams to a lineup that includes Sick New World and Sonic Temple festivals.

item.title: Korn Kicks Off 2024 Tour with a Nostalgic Setlist in Tampa
item.description: Korn’s North American tour kicked off last night, and for those of us who’ve been around long enough to remember them actually playing these songs when they first dropped, it was a bit of a nostalgia trip—whether we asked for it or not.

item.title: MIKE SHINODA Explains Why LINKIN PARK Kept Their Name: "Changing It Would Be Stupid"
item.description: Linkin Park is back, and the headlines are practically writing themselves. New vocalist? Emily Armstrong. New album? From Zero. New tour? It’s happening. But of course, with all this change, the question isn’t just what they’re doing—it’s why.

item.title: Is Lzzy Hale the Future Voice of Linkin Park? Fans Think So
item.description: Linkin Park has been pulling some real grade-A stunts lately. Countdowns leading to… more countdowns. Announcements that announce other announcements. It’s like watching a toddler try to explain a magic trick—it’s messy, pointless, and you’re not even mad, just confused.

item.title: Linkin Park Countdown Ends: What Does 'Be Part of Something' Mean?
item.description: It all started with that bizarre 100-hour countdown plastered across Linkin Park’s socials and website last week. For those who missed the memo, this wasn’t your standard “big announcement” fare—it was more like staring at a ticking clock and wondering if someone accidentally pressed the wrong button.

item.title: Study Shows Korn Fans Get the Best Value for Their Tickets
item.description: These days, going to a concert is like setting fire to your wallet. Everything is overpriced, and ticket prices are no exception. But who’s ready to fork over an arm and a leg just to stand in a crowd?

item.title: Slipknot Reveals Knotfest Argentina and Chile Lineups; See Details
item.description: Slipknot is packing its bags—and masks—for another jaunt through South America, this time with Brazilian powerhouse drummer Eloy Casagrande on the roster. The Knotfest machine is revving up for Argentina and Chile, hot on the heels of announcing Knotfest Brazil.

item.title: Korn Showed Us the Ropes, Mötley Crüe Wanted Us Off the Stage, Says Jacoby Shaddix
item.description: Touring for over two decades brings a lot of memories—some good, some you’d rather forget. When Jacoby Shaddix and Jerry Horton of Papa Roach sat down with Q101, they didn’t hold back on sharing stories from the road.

item.title: Slipknot’s Clown Misses Sonic Temple Due to Dental Surgery
item.description: Slipknot’s lineup has been feeling a bit like a revolving door lately, hasn’t it? Members coming, members going, and the occasional mystery replacement that leaves fans scratching their heads.

item.title: AS I LAY DYING Delays Album Completion Again; See Details
item.description: Here we are again, AS I LAY DYING has a new album brewing, but don’t hold your breath just yet. Vocalist Tim Lambesis, in an interview with Chaoszine, dished out the details, or at least as much as anyone could get from his roundabout explanations.

item.title: Korn's Brian Welch Introduces New Record Label XOVR Records; VIDEO
item.description: Brian “Head” Welch, the guitarist from Korn, has decided that making loud noises on stage wasn’t quite enough, so he’s now entering the record label world with his latest venture, XOVR Records (that’s “Crossover Records” for those who don’t speak in mysterious abbreviations).

item.title: Metallica Competes for Billboard’s Top Rock Duo/Group Award
item.description: Metallica has snagged two Billboard Music Award nominations this year, a surprising nod from an awards scene that, let’s be honest, usually knows nothing about rock or metal.

item.title: Korn's Next Album in 2024 Could Be Their First Without Fieldy
item.description: Korn apparently has some new sounds brewing for 2024, if guitarist Brian “Head” Welch is to be believed. He recently mentioned on The Joe Kingdom Perspective that there’s “new music coming next year,” though it seems like the band is in some kind of self-imposed exile right now, as he put it, “just doing our own thing.

item.title: Metallica Welcomes Unlikely Guest: A Dog Named Storm at LA Concert
item.description: Los Angeles had an unexpected guest at Metallica’s August 25 concert—an adventurous dog named Storm who, without a ticket or invitation, managed to sneak into SoFi Stadium and settle right in with the crowd.
